findings.issue: 急かす is transitive 'to rush/hurry someone along'; そんなに急かすなよ means 'don't rush ME so much'. 'Don't be in such a hurry' reverses the action (listener hurrying themselves = 急ぐ), contradicting pt 'Não me apressa tanto assim!' and the token gloss 'to rush (someone) along'.
findings.current: Don't be in such a hurry.

findings.issue: Literal mirror omits ひとつ ('one'): jp says ONE source of fulfillment vanished, but lit_en reads as if all motivation vanished (total loss). lit_pt correctly keeps 'um' and the natural en keeps 'one of'.
findings.current: I have the feeling my motivation to do it has vanished.
findings.suggested: I have the feeling one (of my) reasons-for-doing-it has vanished.

findings.issue: 'virar-se-á' is mesoclitic future — literary European Portuguese, banned for pt-BR — and wrongly reflexive (雨になる = 'virar chuva'; 'virar-se' means to turn oneself/get by). Also ', né?' misrenders かしら, which is self-directed wondering already covered by '(será que)'.
雨 is marked by に as the result complement of なる; it is not the subject (the implicit subject is the weather/sky). The 'sujeito/' alternative is wrong and should be dropped.
en drops つまり, the discourse connector this sentence showcases (and which the expl fields analyze); pt keeps 'Ou seja'. Add the connector for jp fidelity and en/pt consistency.
The note's equation is malformed: '変わって + てた = 変わっていた' would concatenate to 変わっててた. It should say 変わっ+て+た forms 変わってた, the contraction of 変わっていた. Same garbled equation in the en note.
findings.current: てる (contração de ている); aqui 変わって + てた = 変わっていた ('tinha mudado / estava mudado')
findings.suggested: てる = contração de ている; 変わっ+て+た forma 変わってた, contração de 変わっていた ('tinha mudado')
